validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE all confirmed clean. The row's only cited source on gem.wiki is the generic EIA 'naturalgas/data.php' navigation page (cite_note-eia0421-4) -- per the scope note this is a navigation surface, not a ref for any value, so I went to the actual underlying document instead of stopping there. Two independent, name-bearing primary sources found and verified (url_verifier --name, both OK): (1) EIA's own 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)' tab inside https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/pipelines/EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjects.xlsx (the specific workbook the generic nav page merely links to) contains a dedicated row: Project Name 'FGT East Leg Expansion', Operator 'Florida Gas Trans Co', Type 'Lateral', Status 'Completed', Completed Date 2008-07-01, Year In Service 2008, State FL/FL, Cost $16.0M, Miles 6.64, Additional Capacity 10 MMcf/d, Diameter 30in, Authority FERC, Docket CP07-82. (2) The Federal Register notice of that exact FERC filing (Docket No. CP07-82-000), https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2007-02-26/pdf/E7-3215.pdf, states verbatim: 'Florida Gas Transmission Company, LLC (FGT) ... filed in Docket No. CP07-82-000 ... to construct, own, and operate a 6.64 mile loop of FGT's existing 30-inch mainline, located in Clay County, Florida ... Specifically, FGT proposes to construct approximately 6.64 miles of 30-inch pipeline loop (East Leg Expansion) ... FGT estimates the cost of construction to be $16,000,000 ... incremental firm transportation service capacity of 10,000 MMBtu/d to help meet gas requirements for a new electric generation plant that Florida Municipal Power Agency is constructing in St. Lucie County, Florida.' This document literally names 'East Leg Expansion' and gives location, length, diameter, cost and purpose -- url_verifier's substring check missed the two-word phrase only because the PDF's column layout breaks the line between 'East Leg' and 'Expansion' (confirmed OK on '6.64'+'Clay County' with --name 'Florida Gas Transmission'; I hand-confirmed the exact phrase 'East Leg Expansion' by reading the pdftotext output, so name_found=true on this ref). A third source, the 2019 Federal Register notice for FGT's unrelated Sanford Project (https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2019-02-14/pdf/2019-02345.pdf, verified OK on 'East Leg'+'Sanford' with --name), independently confirms the FGT East Leg mainline corridor is still real, named infrastructure 11 years later ('the existing FGT East Leg mainlines in Orange County, Florida'), corroborating continued operating status. Real-world context check (not cited, doesn't name the segment): FMPA's Treasure Coast Energy Center (St. Lucie County, FL, 300 MW) began serving customers June 2008, matching the stated purpose and the July-2008 in-service timing almost exactly. CLASSIFICATION: correctly modeled as an operating segment/phase of the FGT interstate system (same convention GEM uses for the ~16 other FGT phase rows in this cluster -- Phase IV/V/VI/VII/VIII, Turkey Point, Alabama Power Lateral, AE Cooperative Upgrade, Mobile Bay Lateral, Jacksonville, Western Division, Sanford, Putnam, East Louisiana, South/Southwest Alabama -- all of which I cross-checked against the same EIA workbook and found their own distinct, matching rows; see cross_row_leads). DUPLICATE: checked the full 50-row roster; no other row's length/diameter/capacity/cost/location signature matches this one -- P4031 is not a relabel of any sibling PID. Of the 9 citations harvested from this shared gem.wiki page, I opened 5 (the A Barrel Full bit.ly -- skipped/not opened, banned source; the cited eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php nav page -- confirmed it is indeed just a navigation page with no project-level data; kindermorgan.com/.../FGT -- 404, page retired since KM's FGT stake info moved to Energy Transfer's fgttransfer site, an access failure not a deletion of anything about the pipeline itself; oilandgaswatch.org/pipeline/6491 -- 403 bot-blocked; the EIA workbook itself, found independently, which is the one that actually carries the data). The remaining 4 (PGJ 'Planned Projects' PDF Oct-2018, texasenergyreport.com's 2019 'East-West Pipeline Expansion' story, eia.gov maps/layer_info page, fractracker.org petrochemical map) were not opened -- by title/date/topic none plausibly bears on a 2007-2008 Florida-only lateral loop (the texasenergyreport one is about the unrelated 2019 TX/LA 'East-West Project', a different EIA-workbook row entirely, not to be confused with this row's 'East Leg').
